_note: Authored help prose (Phase 6.2a). The generator (.References/Help_v2/gen-tours.mjs) merges this over the capture manifest, so regeneration after a recapture never clobbers this copy. Per surface: optional category/tier override, title, intro, and per-region label (optional; falls back to the labelized key) and body. Interface-only: describe what an element does, never name example-story content. No internal code terms. Canadian/British spelling. No em dashes.

chapters-acts.title: Chapters and Acts
chapters-acts.intro: Chapters and acts give your story its larger structure. A chapter collects a run of consecutive scenes; acts gather chapters above them. The coloured column bands behind the canvas show which chapter each scene belongs to.

chapter_1.label: Chapter band
chapter_1.body: A chapter band. Every scene sitting within this coloured column belongs to this chapter. Drag a scene into another band to move it between chapters.

chapter_2.label: Next chapter
chapter_2.body: The following chapter band. Bands run left to right in reading order, so they also show the sequence the chapters fall in.

entity-chain.intro: A character, location, item, or faction does not live in one place: it threads through every scene it appears in, carrying its state from one appearance to the next. Each appearance starts from whatever was true at the previous one, so the entity always arrives at a scene already holding the name, colour, description, attributes, and relationships it had upstream. When you change something at a scene, that change is carried forward and stays in effect at every later appearance until you change it again. This forward-carrying thread is the entity chain, and it is what lets the same person evolve across the whole story without you re-entering their details scene by scene.

chain_wires.label: Chain wires
chain_wires.body: These wires join one appearance of an entity to its next appearance, and their direction is what sets the order of the chain. State travels the way the wires point, so an entity reads its starting state from upstream and carries any change forward to everything wired after it.

recurring_entity.label: Recurring entity
recurring_entity.body: This is the same entity showing up again later in the story, not a fresh copy of it. It inherits everything that was true earlier in the chain, so a change you made at an earlier point is already in effect here without being re-entered.

knowledge-chain.intro: A piece of knowledge is a fact in your story, and awareness is the record of who has learned it and how fully. Both move with the story: once a fact is established or someone learns it at a scene, that stays true from there onward until a later scene changes it. This is what lets you track a secret spreading, or one character knowing something another does not, scene by scene rather than all at once.

awareness.label: Awareness
awareness.body: An awareness indicator shows who is aware of a fact at this point in the story and how fully, carried forward from the scene where they first learned it. Each character's understanding is tracked on its own, so different people can know different amounts at the same moment.

knowledge.label: Knowledge
knowledge.body: A piece of knowledge is a fact in the story that characters can come to learn, such as a secret, a discovery, or a rumour. It exists in its own right, and awareness of it is recorded separately for each character as the story moves forward.

pov-chain.intro: The point-of-view chain is the order your story is actually read in, which can differ from how the scenes are arranged on the canvas. Whenever a character carries the point of view at a scene, that scene joins the reading path. The dashed point-of-view wire threads through those scenes in order, so following it from start to finish gives you the told sequence of your manuscript. Scenes with no point-of-view character sit aside as part of the world but outside that reading order.

pov_first.label: First point-of-view scene
pov_first.body: The opening scene of the reading path. The dashed point-of-view wire begins here and runs forward to the next scene a character is seen through, setting where your story starts being told.

pov_second.label: Next on the path
pov_second.body: The next scene a character carries the point of view in, so it is read at this position in the story. Its place in the told order comes from the dashed wire, not from where it sits on the canvas.

pov_third.label: Later on the path
pov_third.body: A scene further along the reading path. Tracing the dashed wire from one point-of-view scene to the next, all the way to here, lays out the full order your manuscript is read in.

off_path.label: Off-path scene
off_path.body: A scene where no character carries the point of view, so the dashed wire skips past it. It still belongs to your world, but it has no fixed place in the told reading order until a character is seen through it.

relationship-chain.intro: A relationship is not fixed: it begins somewhere, gains and loses members, and shifts in tone and standing as the story goes on. Rather than storing a single snapshot, NarrativeNode records each of these moments at the scene where it happens and carries the result forward from there. This tour shows how that history reads scene by scene: where the relationship starts, where someone joins or leaves, and how a participant's role can change along the way. Reading it at any scene tells you exactly where the relationship stood at that moment.

started.label: Relationship begins
started.body: The scene where the relationship comes into being. From this point onward it exists in the story and its starting set of participants is in effect, until something later changes that.

joined.label: Participant joins
joined.body: Someone becoming part of the relationship at this scene. A join, like a later departure, is pinned to the scene where it happens and carries forward from there, so the relationship's membership at any point is the sum of everyone who has joined and not since left.

roles.label: Roles
roles.body: Each participant's role within the relationship, such as their rank or standing. A role can be changed at a later scene, and the role shown here is the one in effect at the point on the story you are viewing rather than a single fixed label.

scene-flashback.intro: A flashback scene depicts events from an earlier time than the moment at which the reader encounters it. It is anchored to a parent scene and shows that scene's cast and their state as it stood there, so you can revisit an earlier beat without breaking the forward order of the rest of your story. Because it looks back rather than carrying the story onward, a flashback is read-only: it reflects what was already established and adds no new changes of its own.

flashback_scene.label: Flashback marker
flashback_scene.body: Marks this scene as a flashback, set apart from a scene sitting in straightforward sequence. It signals that the scene revisits an earlier point in the story, drawing its cast and their state from the parent scene it looks back to rather than from the scenes around it on the canvas.

scene-node.intro: A scene is the basic building block of your story on the canvas: a single beat or moment. It gathers everything that matters at that point, the title, a short description, the characters and other entities present, and any knowledge in play. Scenes connect to one another by wires, and the path those wires trace is how your story moves forward.

node.label: Scene
node.body: The scene as a whole. Everything inside it belongs to this one moment in the story. Where the scene sits on the canvas is just for your own layout; what actually orders your story is the wires running between scenes, not their position.

header.label: Title bar
header.body: Names the scene and is where you select it. The title is what you will recognise it by elsewhere, in the table of contents and the timeline, so a short, telling name helps. This bar also carries the buttons to open the scene in the text editor and to remove it.

description.label: Description
description.body: A short summary of what happens here, shown right on the canvas so you can read the gist without opening anything. The full prose for the scene lives in the editor; this is the at-a-glance version that keeps the canvas readable as your story grows.

entities.label: Entities
entities.body: The characters, locations, items, and factions taking part in this scene, each shown as a chip. A chip displays the entity not as it was first defined but as it stands at this point in the story, with any changes carried forward from earlier scenes already applied. Any relationship in effect at this scene appears as a chip here too, alongside the entity and knowledge chips.

knowledge.label: Knowledge
knowledge.body: The pieces of knowledge in play at this scene: facts, secrets, or revelations that characters may or may not be aware of here. Tracking knowledge per scene lets you keep straight who knows what, and when they came to know it, as the story unfolds.

entity-origin.intro: An entity node is where a character, location, item, or faction enters the story. It holds that entity's starting state: its name, type, colour, description, and attributes. From here, that starting state carries forward along the entity's own thread to every scene it appears in, until a scene changes something. Think of it as the entity's home base, the version everything later inherits from.

node.label: Entity node
node.body: The entity node as a whole. It defines the entity's starting state, the baseline every later appearance inherits from, and is the place to set that baseline up before the entity ever reaches a scene.

header.label: Name and type
header.body: The entity's name and type. Its colour and icon, shown here, identify it wherever it appears across the canvas.

attributes.label: Attributes
attributes.body: The entity's attributes, the defining facts being tracked about it. The values shown here are its starting values, carried forward to later scenes until one of them changes a value.

description.label: Description
description.body: The entity's description. Like its attributes, this is the starting text, in effect until a later scene gives the entity a new description.

group-node.intro: A group is a labelled box you draw around related nodes to tidy the canvas. As a container it is a purely visual aid: it does not change the order your story is told in or affect any entity's state, it just keeps clusters of scenes or entities together so a sprawling canvas stays readable and easy to move around. A group also carries concept ports, so the whole box can be wired into the concept map alongside concept notes.

node.label: Group node
node.body: The group box itself. Drag its header and everything currently sitting inside the box moves with it, so you can shift a whole cluster of scenes or entities at once without disturbing how they connect. Deleting the group leaves its contents on the canvas untouched.

body.label: Grouped area
body.body: The translucent interior of the box. Whatever nodes you position inside its bounds count as part of the group and travel with it, but clicks pass straight through to those nodes so you can still select and edit them normally.

header.label: Group label
header.body: The coloured bar at the top, where you name the group and set its colour. A clear label marks what the enclosed nodes have in common, such as a chapter, an act, or a set of characters that belong together.

ports.label: Concept ports
ports.body: The eight triangle ports a group carries for the concept map, one at each corner and one on the middle of each edge. Hidden until you hover or select the group, they let you wire the whole box to concept notes and to other groups, so a cluster can take part in your brainstorming links. They never affect the story, the reading order, or what the group contains.

knowledge-origin.intro: A knowledge node is the canvas home of a single fact in your story: a secret, a rumour, or a revelation you want to follow. It marks where that fact enters the story and holds its defining name, colour, and description. From here you wire the knowledge out to the characters and scenes it touches, and each observer's awareness of it is tracked separately, so you can show exactly who knows what at any point.

port.label: Output port
port.body: The point you drag a wire from to grant awareness of this fact. Connect it to a character at their starting point or to a character within a scene, and that character becomes aware of the knowledge from that point in the story forward.

header.label: Name and colour
header.body: The knowledge's name and identifying colour, which is how this fact is recognized everywhere it is referenced. Clicking opens the detail panel, where you can review and adjust the knowledge and who is aware of it.

body.label: Details
body.body: The defining description of the fact: what it actually is. This is the starting account of the knowledge, carried forward through the story unless a later scene revises it.

modifier.intro: A modifier is a small change applied to one entity at a point between two scenes, without belonging to a scene itself. Use it when something happens to an entity off the page: an item is destroyed, a character is wounded, a place falls into ruin. It alters a value, and that change carries forward to every scene that follows it along the entity's thread.

badge.label: Change badge
badge.body: Marks this as a modifier and shows the kind of change it makes to the entity at this point. It is the way a change can happen between scenes rather than inside one, with the new value carried forward from here on.

in_port.label: Input port
in_port.body: Where the entity's thread arrives from the scene before it. The state coming in is what the modifier is about to change.

out_port.label: Output port
out_port.body: Where the entity's thread leaves, now carrying the changed value. It connects on to the scenes that follow, all of which inherit the change.

pov-origin-node.intro: The point-of-view origin is a small starting marker on the canvas that says where your story begins being told. From it runs the dashed point-of-view wire, which threads forward through the scenes in reading order. It holds no characters or text of its own; it simply anchors the start of that reading path, and there is one for the story.

badge.label: Point-of-view badge
badge.body: Marks the very start of the reading path. The dashed point-of-view wire leaves here and runs to your first point-of-view scene, so this is where the told order of your story begins.

reference-node.intro: A reference node is a free-standing card you can park anywhere on the canvas to keep supporting material close to the work: a mood image, a research note, a reminder, or a tagged scrap you want to find again later. A third kind, the concept note, adds connection ports so you can wire ideas into a loose map of their own. Every kind is for your eyes only and stays outside the story itself, so it never joins an entity's or relationship's history and never affects what gets exported. Think of it as a sticky note pinned to the board rather than a beat in the plot. Drop as many as you like, colour and tag them, and arrange them wherever they help.

node.label: Reference node
node.body: The card as a whole: a place to keep a note, a piece of media, or a concept note beside your story without it taking part in the narrative. You can move, resize, and collapse it freely, and nothing on it is carried forward to any scene.

header.label: Title
header.body: The reference's title and its colour swatch. The colour is purely for your own visual sorting on the canvas, letting you group related cards at a glance; the title can be left blank when the content speaks for itself.

tags.label: Tags
tags.body: Labels you attach to this reference so it can be grouped and filtered alongside others that share the same tag. They make a scattered set of cards searchable when your canvas fills up.

body.label: Content
body.body: The reference's actual material: either free note text or an attached image or media file. This is the supporting content you want on hand, kept entirely separate from your scenes and entities.

concept-node.title: Concept Node
concept-node.intro: A concept node is a reference card built for brainstorming. Like any reference card it holds a title, a colour, and free text and stays entirely outside your story, but it also carries connection ports so you can wire concepts to one another and to groups. Use them to sketch how ideas, themes, or possibilities relate before any of it becomes a scene. The links are a loose map for your own planning; they never touch an entity's history, the reading order, or what gets exported.

node.label: Concept node
node.body: The card itself: a title, a colour, and free text, the same as a plain note, but marked as a concept and fitted with connection ports. It lives outside the story and never affects any scene, entity, or export; it is purely a place to hold an idea while you map how it relates to others.

header.label: Title and colour
header.body: The top bar: a colour chip, the concept badge, and the title. Set the colour to sort your concepts at a glance on the canvas, and name the idea in the title, which can stay blank while the concept is still just a placeholder.

tags.label: Tags
tags.body: Labels you attach to this concept so it can be grouped and filtered alongside other cards that share a tag. Useful for sorting a board full of loose ideas once it fills up.

body.label: Notes
body.body: The concept's free text: jot down the idea, a question, or anything worth remembering about it. Like the rest of the card it stays outside the story and is never exported.

ports.label: Concept ports
ports.body: Eight triangle ports, one at each corner and one on the middle of each edge. They stay hidden until you hover or select the node, or while a concept wire is being drawn, then appear so you can start or receive a link. Any port can connect to any other; a port points inward until you drag a wire out of it, when it turns to point outward. Every port behaves the same, so use whichever sits closest to where the wire should run.

wire.label: Concept wire
wire.body: The link between two concepts, drawn as a dashed line of small open rings. Each end is tinted the colour of the node at the far end, so the colour near a node signposts where the wire leads. Concept wires only ever join concept notes and groups to one another; they cannot connect to scenes or entities, keeping this idea map cleanly separate from the story.

relationship-origin.intro: A relationship node is where a relationship begins: it names the bond, gives it a colour, and gathers the entities it connects. This is its starting point, the state every later scene inherits and builds on. From here the relationship's story is followed forward as participants join, leave, take on roles, or come to see one another differently at the scenes where those changes happen.

header.label: Name and colour
header.body: The relationship's name and colour, which set how it reads on the canvas and in the chips that mark it at each scene. If you leave the name blank, a label is built automatically from the participants taking part.

participants.label: Participants
participants.body: The entities bound together in this relationship, shown as small avatars, in their starting arrangement. This is the relationship's beginning; later comings and goings are recorded at the scenes where they occur rather than changed here.

canvas-overview.intro: This is the main NarrativeNode workspace and the map for the rest of this help. The canvas in the centre is where you lay out your story: scenes sit as nodes connected by wires, and the entities in them (characters, locations, items, factions) carry their changing state forward from one scene to the next. The menu bar and toolbar run along the top, the side panels hold your library, detail view, and text editor, and the corner controls and minimap help you navigate. Click any highlighted section to learn more about it.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.body: The open canvas where your whole story lives. Drag the background to pan, scroll to zoom, and place scenes and entities anywhere you like. Position is for your own clarity; reading order comes from how scenes are connected, not where they sit.

add_to_canvas.label: Add to canvas
add_to_canvas.body: Open the menu to add something new: a scene, an entity such as a character or location, or another node type. This is the main starting point for building out your story.

toolbar.label: Toolbar
toolbar.body: The canvas toolbar, gathering the everyday building actions: add a node, step back and forward through your edits, and switch how the canvas is laid out.

undo_redo.label: Undo and redo
undo_redo.body: Step backward and forward through your recent canvas edits. Changes are tracked as you work, so you can confidently try a layout or a story change and reverse it if you change your mind.

layout_mode.label: Layout mode
layout_mode.body: Switch between a single row of chapters and a wrapped multi-row arrangement. Multi-row becomes available once you have at least two chapters and helps a long story fit on screen by stacking chapter columns into rows.

canvas_controls.label: Canvas controls
canvas_controls.body: The cluster of view controls in the canvas corner: zoom, fit the whole story into view, lock the layout, choose which wires are shown, snap nodes to a grid, auto-tidy the arrangement, and toggle the minimap.

minimap_resize.label: Minimap resize
minimap_resize.body: Drag this handle on the minimap's corner to make the overview larger or smaller. The size you choose is remembered for next time.

minimap.label: Minimap
minimap.body: A small overview that maps the entire canvas and marks the part you are currently viewing, so you can keep your bearings and jump around a large story quickly. Drag its corner handle to resize it.

canvas-controls.intro: These controls sit in the corner of the canvas and govern how you view and arrange your story rather than what it contains. Use them to zoom, frame the whole narrative, lock the layout while you read, choose which connecting wires are drawn, tidy node positions, and toggle the overview map. Nothing here changes the story itself, only how you look at it.

zoom_in.label: Zoom in
zoom_in.body: Move the view closer so you can read a single scene or entity and its wires in detail.

zoom_out.label: Zoom out
zoom_out.body: Pull the view back to take in more of the story at once, useful for seeing how scenes flow across chapters.

fit_view.label: Fit view
fit_view.body: Frame the entire story on screen at once, bringing every scene and entity into view. A quick way to get your bearings after panning far into one corner.

interactivity.label: Lock canvas
interactivity.body: Lock the canvas so nodes stay put while you read or review. With it unlocked, you can drag nodes freely; locking prevents accidentally nudging your layout out of place.

wire_visibility.label: Wire visibility
wire_visibility.body: Choose which connecting wires are drawn. Show every wire, hide them all, or pick one of two in-between modes, chosen kinds only, or the current selection's wires plus chosen kinds, then tick which wire kinds to include: point of view, narrative, or concept. On a busy canvas this lets you trace one thread without the rest crowding the view.

snap_to_grid.label: Snap to grid
snap_to_grid.body: When on, nodes align to an invisible grid as you drag, keeping scenes and entities neatly squared up. Ctrl+clicking the button instead snaps every existing node to the grid at once. Since a node's position is for your own clarity and does not affect the story, this is purely about a tidy workspace.

reorganize.label: Reorganise
reorganize.body: Automatically tidy the whole canvas: scenes are packed into their chapter columns and each entity's starting node is placed near where it first appears. A fast reset when the layout has drifted into a tangle.

minimap_toggle.label: Minimap toggle
minimap_toggle.body: Show or hide the minimap, the small overview that maps the entire canvas and shows where your current view sits within it. Handy for jumping around a large story.

menu-bar.intro: The menu bar runs across the top of the window and stays in view as you work. On the left it carries the application menu and the application's name; in the middle it shows the current story's title and the file you are saving to; and along the way it gathers quick ways to open the table of contents, the timeline, find and replace, help, and to save. Indicators at the far right keep you posted on connections and on anything the application wants to flag.

wordmark.label: Wordmark
wordmark.body: The application's name and logo, marking the home corner of the window. It is a label rather than a button.

menu_bar.label: Menu bar
menu_bar.body: The whole strip across the top of the window. Everything you reach often without opening a panel lives here: the application menu, the story title and file, and the row of quick actions.

app_menu.label: Application menu
app_menu.body: Opens the main menu for working with files and the application as a whole: starting a new story, opening or saving one, importing and exporting, settings, and help. Recently opened stories also appear here for quick return.

toc.label: Table of contents
toc.body: Opens a structured outline of your story by act, chapter, and scene, following the order it will read in rather than where the scenes happen to sit on the canvas. It is the quickest way to jump straight to a particular scene.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.body: Opens the timeline, which lays your scenes out along the order the story is told in, set by the point of view path. It gives you a single running view of the narrative from beginning to end.

find.label: Find and replace
find.body: Searches the text of your scenes and lets you replace what it finds across the whole story at once. Handy when a name or a wording needs to change everywhere it appears.

help.label: Help
help.body: Turns on help mode: the cursor takes on a question mark, and the next thing you click opens help about that part of the application instead of doing its usual job. A quick way to ask what is this without hunting through a manual.

save.label: Save
save.body: Writes your story to its file. A small mark on the button tells you when there are changes not yet saved, and the button turns green for a moment after a save so you know it went through.

story_title.label: Story title
story_title.body: Shows your story's title in the centre of the bar. Click it to rename the story right here, without opening settings.

mcp_status.label: MCP status
mcp_status.body: Shows whether an outside assistant is connected and currently allowed to work on your story, and flags when one is asking to make changes. Click it to open the control where you grant, deny, or end that access.

alerts.label: Alerts
alerts.body: Gathers notes the application has raised about your story: validation warnings, time gaps in the sequence, and other things worth a glance. Nothing here blocks your work; it is a list you address at your own pace.

active_file.label: Current file
active_file.body: Names the file your story is being saved to, so you always know which project is open. It stays empty until the story has been saved to a location.

wire-visibility.intro: Wires are the lines that connect your scenes and entities on the canvas: they carry the flow from one scene to the next, trace each character or object through the story, and link concept notes into a loose map. On a busy board those lines can crowd the view, so this control chooses how many are drawn at once. Show every wire, hide them all, or pick one of the two in-between modes and then tick which kinds of wire you want, point of view, narrative, or concept, so only the threads that matter right now are drawn.

mode_show_all.label: Show all wires
mode_show_all.body: Draws every wire at once: scene-to-scene flow, each entity's thread, the point-of-view path, relationships, and concept links. This is the default and gives you the complete picture of how everything is wired together.

mode_chosen.label: Chosen only
mode_chosen.body: Shows only the kinds of wire you tick in the boxes below and hides the rest. Use it to focus on one or two layers, for example just the point-of-view path, or just concept links, without the other lines getting in the way.

mode_selection_chosen.label: Selection + chosen
mode_selection_chosen.body: Shows the wires touching whatever you currently have selected, a scene and its threads, or a single entity, relationship, or knowledge, and adds the ticked wire kinds on top. It combines a close look at one element with whichever layers you always want in view.

mode_hide_all.label: Hide all wires
mode_hide_all.body: Hides every wire so only the nodes remain, leaving an uncluttered board for arranging or reviewing. A wire reappears only while you are actively drawing a new one.

type_pov.label: POV
type_pov.body: One of the wire-kind boxes shown under the two chosen modes. Tick it to include the point-of-view path: the wire that threads through the scenes told from a viewpoint character and so sets the order the story reads and exports. Untick it to drop that path from the view.

type_narrative.label: Narrative
type_narrative.body: One of the wire-kind boxes shown under the two chosen modes. Tick it to include the narrative wires: the scene-to-scene flow, the threads tracing entities through the story, and the relationship links between them. Untick it to hide those while keeping the other kinds you have chosen.

type_concept.label: Concept
type_concept.body: One of the wire-kind boxes shown under the two chosen modes. Tick it to include the concept wires: the loose links between concept notes and groups that you use for brainstorming, kept separate from the story itself. Untick it to hide them.

wire_visibility_button.label: Wire visibility
wire_visibility_button.body: Opens this control and shows the mode in effect on its icon. Reach for it whenever the canvas feels crowded to dial the wires down to just the connections you want to focus on.

detail-panel.intro: The detail panel is your reading lens on a single object: whatever you select on the canvas, an entity, a scene, a relationship, or a Knowledge, opens here. Because nothing in NarrativeNode is edited in one global place, this panel always shows the object as it stands at one point in the story, with its starting state and every change carried forward to that point already worked out for you. The navigation bar steps through the object's own points or up to the scene around it, and the sub-tabs split the view into details, attributes, relationships, and who is aware of what.

nav.label: Navigation bar
nav.body: Moves you through the object's life in the story without changing your selection. Step back and forward through the points where this object changes, or step up to the scene that contains it, and the rest of the panel re-reads itself for wherever you land.

pov_nav_toggle.label: Follow point of view
pov_nav_toggle.body: Ties the step-back and step-forward controls to the point-of-view path, so moving through an entity follows the order a reader would meet it rather than every point where it happens to change. Useful when you want to walk the story as it is told, not as it is wired.

nav_up.label: Go up
nav_up.body: Rises from an entity to the scene it sits in, so you can see the whole moment around it: the other characters, the place, the items present. It is the way back out to context after you have followed a single thread down.

nav_first.label: First point
nav_first.body: Jumps straight to where this object begins: its starting state, before any change in the story has touched it. This is the baseline that every later point builds on.

nav_prev.label: Previous
nav_prev.body: Moves one point earlier in this object's story, to the change just before the one you are reading. Each step peels back the most recent change so you can see what the object was before it.

nav_position.label: Position
nav_position.body: Tells you where you are along the object's run of changes and how many points there are in total, so you always know whether you are near its first appearance or its last.

nav_next.label: Next
nav_next.body: Moves one point later in this object's story, to the next moment where something about it changes. Stepping forward applies that change on top of everything carried in from earlier.

nav_last.label: Last point
nav_last.body: Jumps to the most recent point in this object's story, its state as it finally stands after every change has been applied.

nav_focus.label: Focus on canvas
nav_focus.body: Centres the canvas on whatever the panel is currently showing, so you can find it among your scenes and wires without hunting. A quick bridge between reading an object here and seeing where it lives in the story.

header.label: Header
header.body: Names the object you are looking at and marks its kind, with the controls that belong to it as a whole. It stays fixed while you scroll, so you never lose track of what the panel is about.

header_type.label: Type
header_type.body: Marks what kind of object this is, by icon and colour: a character, location, item, faction, custom entity, scene, relationship, or Knowledge. The colour is the object's own, so it reads the same here as on the canvas.

header_name.label: Name
header_name.body: The object's name as it stands at the point you are viewing. Because a name can change over the course of a story, this can differ from the name at the object's first appearance, and the panel always shows the version that applies here.

subtabs.label: Sub-tabs
subtabs.body: Split the object into the views that matter for a story: its core details, its attributes, the relationships it takes part in, and who is aware of it. Each view reads the object at the same point in the story you have navigated to.

body.label: Body
body.body: The working area of the panel, showing whichever sub-tab you have open. Everything here is read and edited for the one point in the story you are at, not for the object in the abstract.

details_description.label: Description
details_description.body: The object's description as it reads at this point in the story. Edit it at the object's start to set its baseline, or at a later scene to record how the description has changed from there forward.

attributes_attributes.label: Attributes
attributes_attributes.body: The entity's attributes as they stand at this point. Each row is one attribute with its name, a badge for its kind, and its current value below: some set right here, others carried forward from earlier in the story.

relationships_body.label: Relationships
relationships_body.body: The relationships this entity is part of at this point in the story. Each row names the other side and the role this entity plays, drawn from the relationship's own history up to here, so you see only the ties that are live at this moment.

relationship_row.label: Relationship
relationship_row.body: A single relationship the entity belongs to, showing the other participant and this entity's role within it. Open it to follow the relationship's own story of how the two sides came together and how they see each other.

attributes_awareness.label: Manage awareness
attributes_awareness.body: Opens the awareness controls for these attributes, where you record who knows each one at this point in the story. Awareness is its own layer over an attribute, so a secret stays hidden from some characters even after it is true.

attributes_attributes_add.label: Add attribute
attributes_attributes_add.body: Adds a new attribute to the entity. Added at its start it becomes part of the baseline that carries forward; added at a later scene it marks the moment the entity gained that trait, applying from there onward.

attribute_type.label: Type badge
attribute_type.body: Tells you what kind of value the attribute holds: text for free writing, preset for a value picked from one of your lists, or file for an attached image, audio, or video. The kind decides how the value is entered and shown.

attribute_change.label: Change indicator
attribute_change.body: Marks an attribute that was changed at the point you are viewing rather than carried in unchanged from earlier: green for added, amber for modified, red for removed. It is how you tell a fresh edit here from inherited state.

attribute_remove.label: Remove
attribute_remove.body: Removes the attribute from this point in the story forward, recording that the entity no longer has it from here on. Earlier scenes keep it, since a removal applies only onward from where you make it.

relationship_add.label: Add relationship
relationship_add.body: Starts a relationship between this entity and another. The tie becomes part of the story from the point you create it, so the two sides are shown as connected from here forward.

details_aliases.label: Aliases
details_aliases.body: The other names this object goes by at this point in the story: cover names, titles, epithets. Aliases are tracked through the story too, so a name a character takes on later appears only from the scene it is adopted.

details_tags.label: Tags
details_tags.body: Labels you put on the object to group and filter it across the story, such as marking a cast of villains or a set of locations in one region. Tags are for your own organisation and carry no narrative meaning of their own.

attributes_circumstances.label: Circumstances
attributes_circumstances.body: The situations the entity is in at this point: things that are simply true of them right now, like wounded, in disguise, or far from home. They sit apart from lasting attributes because they describe a state, not a fixed trait, and they carry forward until you change them.

attributes_circumstances_add.label: Add circumstance
attributes_circumstances_add.body: Adds a circumstance that holds from this point in the story forward. At a scene a second button adds one that applies only there, for a state that is true in that single moment and does not carry on.

details_changes.label: Changes here
details_changes.body: Gathers everything that was changed at this point, set apart from the state carried in from earlier in the story. It is a quick read of what this scene actually does to the object, rather than what it inherits.

attributes_motivators.label: Motivators
attributes_motivators.body: What is driving the entity at this point: the wants, loyalties, and fears pushing them toward what they do. Each motivator can carry an intensity, so you can show a drive that smoulders early and burns by the climax, and each carries forward until you change it.

attributes_motivators_add.label: Add motivator
attributes_motivators_add.body: Adds a motivator that holds from this point in the story forward. At a scene a second button adds one that applies only there, for a drive that flares in that single moment and does not carry on.

motivator_intensity.label: Intensity
motivator_intensity.body: How strongly the motivator weighs on the entity right now, on a scale from faint to intense, shown by its marker. Because intensity is tracked through the story, the same drive can grow or fade from scene to scene.

attributes_perspectives.label: Perspectives
attributes_perspectives.body: How this entity sees something else at this point: their read on another character, a relationship, or a piece of Knowledge. Perspectives let two characters hold opposite views of the same thing, and like everything here they can shift as the story moves on.

attributes_perspectives_add.label: Add perspective
attributes_perspectives_add.body: Adds a perspective: this entity's view of a chosen target, holding from this point in the story forward. It is how you record that a character starts to trust, suspect, or misread someone or something at a given moment.

notes_button.label: Notes
notes_button.body: Opens free-form notes you keep about this object: planning, reminders, and ideas that live alongside the story without being part of it. Notes belong to the object as a whole, not to any one point in the story.

detail-shared.title: Changes at This Point
detail-shared.intro: Across every detail view, this section gathers what changed at the point you are viewing: the values set here, distinct from those carried forward from earlier in the chain.

changes_at_point.label: Changes at this point
changes_at_point.body: The changes recorded at this point in the chain: additions and edits made here, separate from inherited state.

detail-character.intro: This panel shows one character as they stand at a chosen point in the story. A character is not fixed: they begin from a starting state and change as the story moves forward, and this panel always reflects the state in effect at the point you have selected. The sub-tabs across the top split that picture into the character's details, attributes, relationships, and who is aware of what.

header.label: Header
header.body: Identifies the character you are looking at: their name, the fact that they are a character, and their colour, all as they stand at the selected point in the story. If any of these were changed earlier in the narrative, the values shown here are the ones carried forward to this point.

details_tab.label: Details tab
details_tab.body: The Details sub-tab, shown here. It covers the character's descriptive identity at this point: their description, any aliases they go by, and the tags filed against them.

attributes_tab.label: Attributes tab
attributes_tab.body: Switches to the Attributes sub-tab, which lists the character's attributes as they stand at this point in the story. Attributes are the trackable facts about a character, such as age or rank, that can change as the narrative unfolds.

relationships_tab.label: Relationships tab
relationships_tab.body: Switches to the Relationships sub-tab, showing the connections this character has with others at this point: who they know, how each side sees the other, and any groups they belong to. Relationships answer who knows whom and how that stands here.

awareness_tab.label: Awareness tab
awareness_tab.body: Switches to the Awareness sub-tab, which tracks who knows what about this character at this point: who is aware of them, their attributes, or their aliases, and who is deliberately kept in the dark. It is how you keep track of secrets and reveals across the story.

content.label: Content
content.body: The body of the Details sub-tab: the character's description, the aliases they are known by, and their tags, all as they stand at the selected point in the story. Editing a value here records the change from this point forward rather than rewriting the character everywhere.

detail-entity.intro: This panel shows one entity, an item here, as it stands at a chosen point in the story. An entity is not fixed: it begins from a starting state and can change as the narrative moves forward, and this panel always reflects the state in effect at the point you have selected. The navigation bar and sub-tabs let you move along the entity's story and split its picture into details, attributes, relationships, and awareness.

nav.label: Navigation bar
nav.body: Moves the panel through the entity's story: step back and forward across the points where it changes, or jump up to the scene that contains it. The position you land on is the point whose state the rest of the panel reflects.

header.label: Header
header.body: Identifies the entity you are looking at: its name, type, and colour as they stand at the selected point in the story. If any of these were changed earlier in the narrative, the values shown here are the ones carried forward to this point.

details_tab.label: Details tab
details_tab.body: The Details sub-tab, shown here. It covers the entity's descriptive identity at this point: its description, any aliases it goes by, and the tags filed against it.

attributes_tab.label: Attributes tab
attributes_tab.body: Opens the Attributes sub-tab, which lists the entity's attributes as they stand at this point in the story. Attributes are the trackable facts about the entity that can change as the narrative unfolds.

relationships_tab.label: Relationships tab
relationships_tab.body: Opens the Relationships sub-tab, showing the connections this entity has with others at this point: which entities it is tied to and how those ties stand here. Relationships answer who or what is bound to this entity and how that stands at this point.

awareness_tab.label: Awareness tab
awareness_tab.body: Opens the Awareness sub-tab, which tracks who knows what about this entity at this point: who is aware of it, its attributes, or its aliases, and who is deliberately kept in the dark. It is how you keep track of secrets and reveals across the story.

body.label: Body
body.body: The contents of whichever sub-tab is selected, all shown as they stand at the point in the story you are viewing. Editing a value here records the change from this point forward rather than rewriting the entity everywhere.

detail-faction.intro: The detail panel for a faction, shown as it stands at the point in the story you are viewing. A faction is a group or organisation that gathers members and takes part in the narrative, and like every story element its name, look, and standing can shift as events unfold. The sub-tabs split that picture into its details, its attributes, its membership and other ties, and who is aware of it, each reflecting the state in effect at this point.

nav.label: Navigation bar
nav.body: Steps through the faction's life across the story so you can see it as it was earlier or later, and when you have opened it from a scene, lets you jump up to that scene. The arrows move you between the points where the faction changes; everything below updates to match the point you land on.

header.label: Header
header.body: The faction's name and colour as they stand at this point in the story, with its type shown alongside. Because earlier scenes can rename or recolour a faction and carry that change forward, what you see here is its identity at the moment you are viewing, not a fixed label.

details_tab.label: Details tab
details_tab.body: The Details sub-tab, currently open. It holds the faction's description, any names it goes by, and the tags used to group it.

attributes_tab.label: Attributes tab
attributes_tab.body: Opens the faction's attributes: the facts you track about it, such as its size, base, or allegiance, each with the value it holds at this point in the story.

relationships_tab.label: Relationships tab
relationships_tab.body: Opens the faction's ties to other elements, including its members. A faction keeps a membership list, so this is where you see who belongs to it and how that roster stands at this point in the story.

awareness_tab.label: Awareness tab
awareness_tab.body: Opens who knows the faction exists at this point in the story. Awareness lets you track who is aware of the faction, any entity and not just characters, and who is still in the dark, so you can keep secrets and reveals straight as the plot moves.

body.label: Body
body.body: Shows whichever sub-tab is open, always presenting the faction as it stands at the point in the story you are viewing. Move along the chain in the navigation bar and these contents shift to match that moment.

detail-location.intro: The detail panel for a location, shown as it stands at the point in the story you are viewing. A location is a place in your story, and like every element its name, look, and surroundings can change as the plot moves through it. The sub-tabs split that picture into its details, its attributes, the places and elements it connects to, and who is aware of it, each reflecting the state in effect at this point.

nav.label: Navigation bar
nav.body: Steps through the location across the story so you can see it as it was earlier or later, and when you have opened it from a scene, lets you jump up to that scene. The arrows move you between the points where the location changes; everything below updates to match the point you land on.

header.label: Header
header.body: The location's name and colour as they stand at this point in the story, with its type shown alongside. Because earlier scenes can rename or recolour a place and carry that change forward, what you see here is its identity at the moment you are viewing, not a fixed label.

details_tab.label: Details tab
details_tab.body: The Details sub-tab, currently open. It holds the location's description, any names it goes by, and the tags used to group it.

attributes_tab.label: Attributes tab
attributes_tab.body: Opens the location's attributes: the facts you track about it, such as its climate, ruler, or condition, each with the value it holds at this point in the story.

relationships_tab.label: Relationships tab
relationships_tab.body: Opens the location's ties to other elements, including the places it contains or sits within. Locations can nest inside one another, so this is where you see how this place fits into the wider map at this point in the story.

awareness_tab.label: Awareness tab
awareness_tab.body: Opens who knows the location exists at this point in the story. Awareness lets you track who is aware of the place, any entity and not just characters, and who is not, so a hidden refuge or undiscovered ruin stays secret until you choose to reveal it.

body.label: Body
body.body: Shows whichever sub-tab is open, always presenting the location as it stands at the point in the story you are viewing. Move along the chain in the navigation bar and these contents shift to match that moment.

detail-scene.intro: The detail panel for a scene, the single beat of your story you have selected on the canvas. It gathers everything in play at that moment: a short description of what happens, the entities present, the relationships between them, and any knowledge that is in circulation. Each item listed is a doorway you can step through to see and edit its own state as it stands at this scene.

details_tab.label: Details tab
details_tab.body: The overview of the scene, currently shown. It holds the scene's description and the lists of what is present here: entities, relationships, and knowledge.

circumstances_tab.label: Circumstances tab
circumstances_tab.body: Switches to the conditions colouring this scene, such as the weather, mood, or pressures acting on the characters. These set the backdrop without recording a change to any entity.

changes_tab.label: Changes tab
changes_tab.body: Switches to a summary of everything that changes at this scene: the new values, additions, and removals first recorded here. It is a single place to review what this beat does to your story before the effects carry forward.

details_description.label: Description
details_description.body: A short summary of what happens in this scene, separate from the full prose you write in the editor. It is the at-a-glance note shown on the scene's card on the canvas, useful for keeping the beat clear while you plan.

details_entities.label: Entities
details_entities.body: The characters, locations, items, and other entities present in this scene, grouped by type. Select one to step into its detail and see or edit its state as it stands at this point in the story.

details_relationships.label: Relationships
details_relationships.body: The relationships in play here, drawn from the entities present in this scene. Select one to open its detail at this point, or add a relationship to record a new connection forming at this beat.

details_knowledge.label: Knowledge
details_knowledge.body: The pieces of knowledge circulating at this scene: secrets, facts, or revelations you are tracking. Select one to see its detail here, or anchor a piece of knowledge to mark where it comes into play in the story.

detail-relationship.intro: A relationship is a connection between one or more entities, with its own history that unfolds as the story does. This panel shows that relationship as it stands at the scene you have selected: who takes part, how each of them sees it, and the role each one holds. Edit a value here and the change is recorded at this scene and carried forward to later ones, so the connection can shift, deepen, or break as the narrative moves.

details_body.label: Details
details_body.body: The relationship as it stands at this point in the story. Its description, tags, and participants are shown the way they are at the selected scene, reflecting any changes made up to this point rather than a single fixed definition.

details_tags.label: Tags
details_tags.body: Labels you attach to this relationship so you can group and filter related connections across the story. Tags describe the relationship itself rather than any single scene, which makes them handy for picking out threads like rivalries or alliances later on.

details_participants.label: Participants
details_participants.body: The entities taking part in this relationship at the selected scene. Because participants can join or leave over the course of the story, this list reflects who is involved at this point and not who has ever been involved.

details_participant_row.label: Participant
details_participant_row.body: One entity's stake in the relationship, showing the role it holds and how it sees the connection at this point. Expand it to set that participant's own view of the relationship, choose which of its names is in play here, and assign a role; those settings are recorded at this scene and carried forward.

details_add_participant.label: Add participant
details_add_participant.body: Brings another entity into this relationship from this scene onward. The entity joins as of this point in the story and remains a participant in later scenes, leaving earlier scenes untouched.

detail-knowledge.intro: The Details sub-tab for a piece of knowledge. A knowledge is a specific fact in your story, such as a secret, a rumour, or a revelation, that you want to keep track of as it spreads. This tab is where you write down what that fact actually is and tag it, while a separate awareness view tracks who has come to know it at each point in the story.

details_body.label: Details
details_body.body: Spells out what the fact is, in your own words. This is the heart of the knowledge: the description you write here is the thing characters may or may not know, and it can be linked to the moment in the story where it first comes to light.

details_tags.label: Tags
details_tags.body: Tags placed on this fact so you can group and find related pieces of knowledge later. They are an organising aid for you, not something the characters in the story see or react to.

chat-panel.intro: The chat panel is your conversation channel with the AI about your story, docked beside the canvas so you can talk while you plan. It holds your saved conversations and the running thread, and the AI can read from and act on your story through it. This is also where character chats appear, letting one of your characters answer in their own voice.

header.label: Header
header.body: Names the active conversation and gathers its controls in one strip: which connection and model are answering, and toggles for how messages are shown. For a character chat it instead shows who you are talking with and the point in the story they are speaking from.

close.label: Close
close.body: Hides the chat panel and returns the full width to the canvas. Your conversations are kept, so reopening the panel brings the active thread back exactly as you left it.

content.label: Content
content.body: The conversation itself: the back-and-forth of messages with the AI, newest at the bottom. When no thread is open this area lists your saved conversations so you can pick one up or start a new one.

conversation.intro: A single conversation with the AI. The thread above holds the exchange so far, and the composer below is where you write your next message. Because the AI does not see your story unless you show it, the composer is also where you decide what context travels with each message: the scene in focus, specific entities or relationships, or an attached file.

thread.label: Message thread
thread.body: The running exchange between you and the AI, oldest at the top and newest at the bottom. This is the record of the conversation; it grows as you send messages and the AI replies.

composer.label: Composer
composer.body: The area where you compose your next message and decide what story context goes with it. Everything here feeds one outgoing message: the text you type, plus any scenes, entities, or relationships you choose to attach so the AI can reason about them.

composer_input.label: Message box
composer_input.body: Where you type the message you want to send. As you write, your story's entity names can be highlighted here so you can see at a glance which ones the AI will recognize when context is attached.

composer_send.label: Send
composer_send.body: Sends your message, together with any attached context, to the AI and waits for its reply. The exchange then joins the thread above.

composer_settings.label: Composer settings
composer_settings.body: Chooses which connection and model answer you, the system prompt that frames how the AI behaves, and how far back through the message history the AI is given. These settings shape every message in this conversation rather than any one of them.

composer_attach_file.label: Attach file
composer_attach_file.body: Attaches a file to this message so the AI can take it into account. Use it when the material you want the AI to see lives outside your story, such as a reference document or an image.

composer_favourites.label: Favourites
composer_favourites.body: Inserts a reusable snippet or prompt you have saved as a favourite. It saves retyping the wordings and instructions you reach for often when working with the AI.

composer_scene_context.label: Pin scene
composer_scene_context.body: Pins the scene currently in focus on the canvas as context, so the AI sees that beat of the story alongside your message. This is the quickest way to ground a question in whatever scene you are working on.

composer_add_context.label: Add context
composer_add_context.body: Opens a picker for choosing exactly what the AI should see with your message: particular scenes, entities, relationships, or markers that resolve to the right point in the story. Because the AI has no view of your story on its own, attaching context here is how it learns who is who and where things stand at this point.

composer_highlight_names.label: Highlight names
composer_highlight_names.body: Highlights your story's entity names in colour as you type in the message box. It gives you a live preview of which characters, places, and other entities the AI could recognize, and you can choose which kinds of names to detect.

composer_auto_attach.label: Auto-attach
composer_auto_attach.body: Automatically attaches the entities you name in your message as context, instead of you adding each one by hand. It keeps the AI aware of who and what you are referring to without interrupting your writing to pin them.

composer_reasoning.label: Reasoning effort
composer_reasoning.body: Sets how hard the model thinks before it answers, on connections and models that support a reasoning setting. More effort can give a more considered reply at the cost of speed.

mcp-control.intro: MCP lets an outside assistant work on your story for you, using the same building blocks you use by hand: it can add scenes, set who is present, record what changes at each point, and adjust relationships. Nothing happens without your say-so. This control shows whether such a connection is open and lets you turn it on or off for the current sitting, and it is also where requests to make changes come in for your approval.

status.label: Status
status.body: Shows at a glance whether an outside assistant can reach NarrativeNode right now and whether it is currently allowed to make changes. This is your reassurance that the door is only open when you have opened it.

turn_on.label: Turn on
turn_on.body: Opens the door for this sitting so an outside assistant can connect and ask to work on your story. It stays off until you choose this, and turning it on here does not change what happens the next time you launch the application.

message-bubble.intro: A single message in the conversation with the AI. Each one carries the text that was exchanged, plus the model and time it was sent. On the AI's replies, a row of actions lets you fold the message back into your story, reuse it, or tidy the thread. The actions appear when you hover over the message.

header.label: Header
header.body: Identifies the message: who sent it, which model produced an AI reply, and when. For replies written in a character's voice, the character's name and colour appear here so you can tell speakers apart at a glance.

body.label: Text
body.body: The message text itself, the actual words exchanged with the AI. Long messages can be collapsed to a short preview so the thread stays readable.

actions.label: Actions
actions.body: The row of actions for this message. These let you bring the message into your story, copy or edit it, reshape the conversation, or remove it. The row appears when you hover over the message.

action_apply.label: Apply to section
action_apply.body: Drops the message text into a section of your story in the editor, either replacing what is there, adding to the end, or adding to the start. This is the main way a passage the AI helped you write becomes part of your manuscript. Available when the editor is open on a section.

action_copy.label: Copy
action_copy.body: Copies the message text to the clipboard so you can paste it anywhere outside the conversation.

action_edit.label: Edit
action_edit.body: Edits the wording of the message in place. On your own messages you can also resubmit the edited version to get a fresh reply; on the AI's messages the edit is text only and does not regenerate the response.

action_collapse.label: Collapse
action_collapse.body: Shrinks a long message to a short preview, or expands it back to full height. Useful for keeping a busy conversation scannable without losing anything.

action_resend.label: Resend
action_resend.body: Sends one of your own messages again to get a fresh reply. If a reply already sits below it, that reply is discarded first so the new one takes its place.

action_favourite.label: Favourite
action_favourite.body: Marks the message as a favourite so you can find and reuse it later. A second click makes it sticky, keeping it close to hand across conversations.

action_retry.label: Retry
action_retry.body: Discards this AI reply and asks the model to answer the same question again, in case a different attempt lands better.

action_fork.label: Fork
action_fork.body: Starts a new thread carrying the conversation up to and including this message, so you can explore a different direction without disturbing the original. The original stays saved in your thread browser.

action_view_context.label: View context
action_view_context.body: Opens the exact background that was sent to the AI alongside this message, such as the scene and any pinned items that were in force at that point. It lets you see what the model could actually draw on when it replied.

action_add_cue.label: Add cue
action_add_cue.body: A planned action, not yet available, so the button stays disabled for now. Once it ships it will let you save a useful part of the message as a reusable context cue, a snippet you can hand to the AI again in later conversations without retyping it.

action_delete.label: Delete
action_delete.body: Removes the message from the conversation. Deleting one of your own messages can also remove the AI reply paired with it.

thread-browser.intro: Every chat you hold with the AI about your story is kept here as its own conversation, so you can return to an earlier thread rather than starting over each time. The list gathers them all in one place: search and filter to find the one you want, open it to pick up where you left off, or begin a fresh thread. Two kinds live side by side here: an open conversation with the assistant, and a character chat, where the AI answers in the voice of one of your characters.

search.label: Search
search.body: Find a conversation by typing part of its name or wording from inside it. The list narrows as you type to just the threads that match, which helps when you have built up many over a long project.

tabs.label: Filter tabs
tabs.body: Narrow the list by which story a conversation belongs to: see them all together, just the ones for the story you currently have open, or those tied to no loaded project. Useful for keeping one story's discussions separate from another's.

more_actions.label: More actions
more_actions.body: Opens a small menu of upkeep actions for the conversation list, such as rebuilding its index if the listing ever looks out of date. These are occasional maintenance tasks rather than everyday use.

select_mode.label: Select
select_mode.body: Switches the list into selection mode so you can tick several conversations and act on them together, such as deleting a batch of old threads in one go. Turn it off to go back to opening conversations with a single click.

threads.label: Conversation list
threads.body: The conversations themselves, with pinned ones gathered at the top and, in the all-stories view, grouped under the story each belongs to. Select any row to open that conversation and continue it.

new_conversation.label: New conversation
new_conversation.body: Starts a fresh chat with the AI about your story. This is the open assistant, used for planning, brainstorming, or asking it to work with your story's details, rather than speaking as any one character.

new_character_chat.label: New character chat
new_character_chat.body: Starts a conversation where the AI answers in the voice of one of your characters, drawing on what that character is like and knows at the point you choose. A short setup step lets you pick the character and the moment in the story before the chat begins.

tool-call-chip.title: Tool Call Chip
tool-call-chip.intro: When the AI uses a tool to act on your story during a reply, its work shows here: its reasoning, its answer, and the tools it called.

header.label: Header
header.body: Marks a reply where the AI used tools.

thinking.label: Reasoning
thinking.body: The AI's reasoning before answering, where the model exposes it.

tool_calls.label: Tool calls
tool_calls.body: The tools the AI called and what each did to your story.

editor-panel.intro: The editor is the right sidebar, where you write a scene's actual prose. A formatting toolbar runs across the top with the usual rich-text controls plus a few writing aids: highlighting the names of your story's entities, finding and replacing text, and a clean light reading view. The scene's short description sits between the toolbar and the writing area, and the word and character counts and a zoom control sit along the foot. The editor follows whichever scene you select on the canvas unless you pin it.

header.label: Header
header.body: Names the scene you are currently writing and holds the editor's panel controls: pinning, the description toggle, and the close button.

scene_description_toggle.label: Prose or description
scene_description_toggle.body: Shows or hides the scene's short description area beneath the toolbar, so you can switch between writing the full prose and noting what the scene is about.

pin_scene.label: Pin scene
pin_scene.body: Pins the editor to this scene so it stays open even as you click other things on the canvas. Without a pin, selecting a different scene switches the editor to that scene's prose; pin when you want to keep writing one scene while exploring the rest of the story.

toolbar.label: Toolbar
toolbar.body: The formatting toolbar for the scene's prose: headings, font and size, inline styles and colours, alignment, lists and blocks, undo and redo, and the writing aids for name highlighting, find and replace, and the light reading view.

heading_1.label: Heading 1
heading_1.body: Formats the current line as a top-level heading.

heading_2.label: Heading 2
heading_2.body: Formats the current line as a second-level heading.

heading_3.label: Heading 3
heading_3.body: Formats the current line as a third-level heading.

font_family.label: Font
font_family.body: Chooses the typeface used to display the prose in the editor.

font_size.label: Text size
font_size.body: Chooses the size of the selected text.

light_mode.label: Light view
light_mode.body: Switches the writing area to a light, page-like reading view, which some writers find easier on the eyes for reading prose back. It changes only how the editor looks to you and does not alter the saved text.

highlight_names.label: Highlight names
highlight_names.body: Tints the names of your story's entities wherever they appear in the prose, so you can see at a glance who and what a scene mentions. Use the small arrow to choose which kinds of entity get highlighted. This is a reading aid only and does not change the text.

text_colour.label: Text colour
text_colour.body: Sets the colour of the selected text from a small palette.

highlight_colour.label: Highlight colour
highlight_colour.body: Applies a highlight colour behind the selected text from a small palette.

strikethrough.label: Strikethrough
strikethrough.body: Strikes a line through the selected text.

align_left.label: Align left
align_left.body: Aligns the paragraph to the left margin.

align_centre.label: Centre
align_centre.body: Centres the paragraph between the margins.

align_right.label: Align right
align_right.body: Aligns the paragraph to the right margin.

align_justify.label: Justify
align_justify.body: Stretches the paragraph to sit flush against both margins.

bullet_list.label: Bulleted list
bullet_list.body: Turns the selected lines into a bulleted list.

numbered_list.label: Numbered list
numbered_list.body: Turns the selected lines into a numbered list.

blockquote.label: Block quote
blockquote.body: Sets the selected text off as an indented block quote.

code_block.label: Code block
code_block.body: Formats the selected text as a fixed-width code block.

horizontal_rule.label: Divider
horizontal_rule.body: Inserts a horizontal divider line, useful for marking a break between passages within a scene.

undo.label: Undo
undo.body: Undoes your last edit in the prose.

redo.label: Redo
redo.body: Redoes the edit you just undid.

insert_section.label: Insert section
insert_section.body: Inserts a section: a labelled block inside the scene's prose that you can treat as a unit, for instance to draft, summarize, or hand a passage to the AI on its own. Use it to break a long scene into named parts you can work on separately.

inline_prompt_block.label: Inline prompt block
inline_prompt_block.body: Drops a prompt block right where the cursor sits, so you can ask the AI to draft prose at that exact point in the scene and have its reply land in place. Once a block is present this same button dismisses it, or stops its response while it is still being written.

find_replace.label: Find and replace
find_replace.body: Opens a panel to search the scene's prose and, if you wish, replace matches with new text. Handy for renaming or rewording something consistently across a scene. The shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+H.

content.label: Writing area
content.body: The main area where you write the scene's prose. This is the scene's actual narrative text, the words a reader would read; it saves automatically as you type. Right-click here for the insert-section and prompt-block options.

footer.label: Footer
footer.body: The bar across the bottom of the editor, holding the word and character counts and the zoom control.

word_count.label: Word count
word_count.body: The number of words in the scene's prose, updating as you write.

character_count.label: Character count
character_count.body: The number of characters in the scene's prose, updating as you write.

zoom_reset.label: Reset zoom
zoom_reset.body: Returns the editor zoom to its default level.

zoom_slider.label: Zoom
zoom_slider.body: Scales the editor's text up or down for comfortable reading, without changing the saved prose. Adjusts in steps between 50% and 200%.

entity-library.intro: The entity library is the left sidebar's catalogue of everything in your story, grouped by type: characters, locations, items, factions, custom entities, knowledge, relationships, tags and lists, context cues, and references. It is where you create new objects and find existing ones, and it shows each object's starting state, the way it stood when first defined. To see how an object has changed at a particular point in the story you switch to the detail view, which reads the state at whatever you have selected on the canvas. Filter within a type, or switch types using the row of tabs.

view_tabs.label: Library or detail
view_tabs.body: Switch the left sidebar between the library, which lists everything in your story, and the detail view, which shows the selected object as it stands at the chosen point in the story.

tab_library_view.label: Library view
tab_library_view.body: Show the library: the catalogue of every object in your story, listed by type. This is where you browse, filter, and create.

library_panel.label: Library panel
library_panel.body: The whole library sidebar. Choose a type with the tabs across the top, narrow it with the filter, and work through the list below.

tab_details_view.label: Detail view
tab_details_view.body: Show the detail view for whatever is selected on the canvas. It reads the object's state at that point in the story, so it reflects changes made earlier in the chain rather than just the starting state shown in the library.

collapse.label: Collapse
collapse.body: Tuck the sidebar away to give the canvas more room. Bring it back from the toolbar when you need it again.

tab_bar.label: Type tabs
tab_bar.body: Choose which kind of object the list shows. Each tab is a separate catalogue: switching tabs changes both the list below and what the New button creates.

tab_character.label: Characters
tab_character.body: List the characters: the people and named beings in your story. Only characters can carry the point of view in a scene.

tab_location.label: Locations
tab_location.body: List the locations: the places and settings in your story. Locations can be nested, so one can sit inside another.

tab_item.label: Items
tab_item.body: List the items: the objects that matter to your story and that you want to track as they move and change.

tab_faction.label: Factions
tab_faction.body: List the factions: the groups and organisations in your story. A faction keeps a membership record so you can track who belongs to it.

tab_custom.label: Custom
tab_custom.body: List your custom entities: your own object types for anything the built-in kinds do not cover. Each one belongs to a category you name, so you can group many of the same sort together.

tab_knowledge.label: Knowledge
tab_knowledge.body: List the pieces of knowledge in your story: facts, secrets, and information you want to track. Knowledge pairs with awareness, which records who knows it and how fully as the story moves on.

tab_relationships.label: Relationships
tab_relationships.body: List the relationships: the connections between entities, and how each side sees the other. A relationship can join two entities or many, and it changes over the course of the story like anything else.

tab_tags_and_lists.label: Tags and lists
tab_tags_and_lists.body: Manage your tags and your preset lists. Tags let you label and filter objects; preset lists give attributes a fixed set of values to choose from, such as a list of species or ranks.

tab_context_cues.label: Context cues
tab_context_cues.body: Manage context cues: reusable notes you can hand to the AI as background. Keep them here so the same guidance is ready to attach whenever you need it.

tab_references.label: References
tab_references.body: List your reference notes: loose notes and media you keep on the canvas for yourself, separate from your story's entities.

filter_input.label: Filter
filter_input.body: Narrow the current list to objects whose name matches what you type. It filters only the type you are viewing, so each tab keeps its own filter.

entity_rows.label: List
entity_rows.body: Every object of the chosen type. Clicking a row opens its detail only when the object already has an origin node on the canvas; a row marked with the empty-set badge is not placed yet, so clicking it does nothing. Drag any row onto the canvas to bring it into a scene.

entity_row.label: Row
entity_row.body: A single object in the list. Click to see its detail, but only when it already has an origin node on the canvas: a row marked with the empty-set badge is not placed yet, so clicking it does nothing. You can still drag it onto the canvas to place it where you want it in the story.

new_entity_btn.label: New
new_entity_btn.body: Create a new object of the type you are currently viewing. It opens a form to name and define the object, and it appears on the canvas ready to wire into your scenes.

entity-modal.intro: The dialog for creating a new entity: a character, location, item, faction, or custom element of your story. What you set here becomes the entity's starting state, the baseline it carries from its origin into every scene it later appears in. The Details tab covers its identity and the Attributes tab covers its defining facts. Nothing here is locked in; you can change any of it later, scene by scene, as the story unfolds.

header.label: Header
header.body: Names the entity being created and lets you close the dialog. It simply frames the work below.

tabs.label: Tabs
tabs.body: Switches between the entity's Details and its Attributes. Details cover who or what it is; Attributes cover the facts you want to track about it.

tab_details.label: Details
tab_details.body: The entity's core identity: its name, type, colour, description, and who is aware it exists. These are the starting values that carry forward through the story.

tab_attributes.label: Attributes
tab_attributes.body: The entity's attributes, the defining facts you want to follow over the story, such as a title, an age, or a piece of equipment. Their starting values are set here and carried forward until a scene changes them.

body.label: Body
body.body: The contents of whichever tab is selected, where you fill in the entity's details or build up its attributes.

name.label: Name
name.body: The entity's name, used to identify it everywhere it appears. For a custom entity this is optional and falls back to an automatic name from its category.

type.label: Type
type.body: What kind of entity this is: character, location, item, faction, or a custom type of your own. The type sets the entity's icon and governs which extra fields appear, such as a parent location or a custom category.

colour.label: Colour
colour.body: The colour that identifies this entity at a glance wherever it shows up across the canvas, on its node, its chips, and its links. Pick from the swatches or enter a specific value.
